mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 9% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive despite UNRATE exceeding 9%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate alongside falling unemployment indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not occur when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rate predicts negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not occur despite FEDFUNDS increase in tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm employment signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow PAYEMS growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption expenditure signals reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not occur despite RSAFS growth slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with low inflation creates a favorable environment for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not occur with GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL conditions met.

mechanism_narrative: Rapid industrial production growth during expansion signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not occur despite INDPRO growth during expansion.
